question.text: Under the SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations 2012, which of the following is EXCLUDED from the definition of an AIF?

explanation.text: The Logic: The SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012 define an AIF as a privately pooled investment vehicle that collects funds from a select group of investors, and explicitly exclude family trusts, ESOP/employee benefit trusts, holding companies, securitisation SPVs, and funds regulated by other regulators from the AIF definition. The Trap: Private equity, venture capital and infrastructure funds are valid AIF examples under the workbook. Family trusts are excluded because they are private vehicles of a family rather than pooled vehicles for select external investors. Note: Use the exclusions on pages 17-18 of the workbook and the valid examples on pages 36-37 and 65; avoid additional claims about family trusts as investors in AIFs that are not separately sourced.
